notes: Corrected: the 'to' of 'to the bank of the river' moves from the causative verb to the noun. Rule 44's supplied-preposition clause requires a bare direct object, but הֵשִׁיב's object is the suffix 'me'; שְׂפַת הַנָּחַל is a directional accusative, which is rule 33's own example ('to your mountain').
'this' after 'hast thou seen' remains added: no object morpheme stands in the clause (rule 44).
The vocative בֶן־אָדָם takes no supplied 'O' here, and its 'of' belongs to the rectum (rules 19, 36).
